rationale: Round 0 compiled, ran correctly, and hit no ICE fallback, so the prudent move is to raise obfuscation intensity across the board rather than hold back. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because instruction substitution is cheap, low-risk, and effective on this program's arithmetic- and comparison-heavy helpers (hashing, string comparison, counting loops). FLA and BCF are pushed moderately high since the spell_checker process function and Rb_tree helpers have enough control flow to flatten and wrap profitably, but their RuntimeCost weights stay below ~0.4 so the tuner does not over-apply them to the hot word-lookup and iteration loops that dominate spellcheck runtime. ICALL is elevated to obscure virtual-like dispatch and library call sites in the spell_checker class methods, while IBR adds control-flow indirection at moderate weight. SPLIT and IGV remain mid-weight support passes: SPLIT mainly helps diversify the few larger functions (spell_checker ctor at 697 bytes, process at 367), and IGV adds global-variable obfuscation without dominating selection. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low across all passes since round 0 showed no correctness or build issues, giving the tuner room to apply passes more broadly while still prioritizing runtime and size restraint on this small (2215-byte text), 11-function benchmark.
